title: Working Safely in Cold Environments
osha_standards: OSH Act Section 5(a)(1) General Duty Clause
summary: Long hours in freezing or cold weather can cause trench foot, frostbite, and hypothermia. This talk covers dressing for the cold, the buddy system, and spotting danger signs.
talking_points: Dress in loose-fitting layers made for cold, wet, and windy weather. Wear a hat, gloves, warm socks, and outerwear that keeps you dry.
Work in pairs so you and your coworker can watch each other for danger signs.
Drink warm, sweet drinks like sugar water or sports drinks. Avoid caffeine and alcohol.
Take breaks often in a heated area to warm up.
Know the danger signs: uncontrolled shivering, slurred speech, clumsiness, fatigue, and confusion.
Get medical help right away if you or a coworker shows signs of hypothermia. Your risk is higher with some medications, poor physical condition, or diabetes, high blood pressure, or heart disease.
site_hazards_to_check: Workers without hats, gloves, or dry, layered clothing
No heated break area on or near the site
Wet or windy conditions that speed up body heat loss
Workers assigned to work alone in the cold
discussion_questions: Is everyone dressed for today's temperature and wind? Who is missing gear?
Who is your buddy today, and what signs are you watching for in each other?
Where is the warm-up area, and how often will we take breaks?
